ideas.title: Give Omar the honest hook number: engagedViews next to views
ideas.problem: youtube.py METRICS (line 37) asks for views, watch time, average view duration/percentage, subs, likes, comments, shares. YouTube's own blog (Aug 24, in watch.json) says Shorts views now count from the first frame, so a Short that most people swipe past still shows a big 'views'. Omar's daily line and weekly note therefore cannot tell 'many saw it' from 'many stayed', and Calina's learning note inherits the blur. The owner's goal is views first, and the hook is the part we can change.
ideas.proposal: In youtube.py add engagedViews to METRICS (a core Analytics API metric: 'viewed past the first frame, or the user clicks/taps to play'; same yt-analytics.readonly scope, no reconnect). In snapshot() keep it per video, and in omar.py add engaged_share = engagedViews / views to the per-video rows, the daily line and the weekly brief (a 'hook' section: lowest and highest engaged_share Shorts with their first line from the episode's script). Add one sentence to OMAR_SYSTEM: 'engaged_share under the channel median means the opening failed; above it with low averageViewPercentage means the middle failed.' If the API refuses engagedViews with dimension=video, fall back to the channel total and say so (the existing code already turns a refusal into an error row for countries, the same pattern works).
ideas.gain: Omar and Calina get a number tied to the opening seconds, with no manual Studio copying. Measure: after 2 weeks, the weekly note names the best and worst opening per Short, and the owner can compare it with Calina's hook styles.
ideas.test: 1) Normal: practice mode (youtube._fake) returns engagedViews; daily line shows 'engaged 62% of views'. 2) Edge: a video with 0 views must not divide by zero and shows '-'. 3) Failure: API returns 400 for engagedViews by video; snapshot still completes and the note says 'hook number unavailable'. Pass = no crash, all three lines read correctly. Then one real snapshot on the live channel.
ideas.confidence_why: The metric's existence and definition are in Google's own metrics page (A). Not verified: whether it can be grouped by video, and whether the Aug 24 views change (YouTube blog, A) makes views and engagedViews diverge enough on our channel to matter.
ideas.risks: Read-only, same scope, no new dependency. Risk: the per-video report may reject the metric, then only the channel total works. Numbers lag 1-2 days like the others.
